title: BRAKE BY
PRESSURE.
NOT TRAVEL.
slides.sub: Why load-cell brakes make braking repeatable.

title: WHAT'S MEASURED.
slides.label: LOAD CELL
slides.body: A load cell reads **how hard** you press. A potentiometer reads **how far** the pedal moves.

before.label: Travel
before.title: A position
before.body: Your foot learns where the pedal is. Hard to hit the same spot at the limit.

after.label: Pressure
after.title: A force
after.body: Your foot learns how hard to push, like the brake in a real race car.

title: SAME PUSH.
SAME BRAKING.
slides.body: The same pressure gives the same braking force, wherever the pedal sits. **The gain is consistency, lap after lap.**

title: NO FLEX.

steps.title: Rigid mounting
steps.body: Pedal plate and seat must not move under load

steps.title: Set the force
steps.body: Max braking at a push you can repeat

steps.title: Practise by feel
steps.body: Brake to pressure, not to a position

slides.body: A pressure brake only works if **the rig doesn't flex** when you push.

title: BRAKE BY FEEL,
NOT DISTANCE.
slides.body: Faster isn't the first win. Being the same every lap is.
